title: Say It Another Way: Auditing LLMs with a User-Grounded Automated Paraphrasing Framework
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured stereotypical bias in model outputs related to the social category of religion, using the 'Religion' subset of the BBQ dataset.
findings: Using the Gemma3-12B model on the BBQ dataset, performance on the 'Religion' subset was sensitive to the type of paraphrase applied. For example, 'Synonym' substitution decreased accuracy by -2.03% while 'Voice Change' increased it by +0.34%. This demonstrates that model behavior in religious contexts is not stable under linguistic variations, and that these specific sensitivities are often masked when using unconstrained or aggregated paraphrasing methods.
